checkout_rails: No live Amazon.com checkout UI was rendered due to storefront access restrictions in the browser environment; evidence relies on official payment-method documentation and observed app-store/marketplace disclosures rather than a live checkout sequence.
value.expectation_copy: “See It On Your Model” (UI label) and the accompanying descriptive copy that the feature can simulate how clothing looks on real models; official guidance also states shoppers can choose from multiple real models and see garments on a model of their choice.
value.gap_vs_onpoint: Gaps identified relative to OnPoint’s positioning include: (1) lack of a local African-fashion supply graph with authentic stock metadata, (2) absence of native local-pay rails (e.g., M-Pesa, WhatsApp commerce) in a buyer-agent workflow, (3) no public buyer-facing agent.json/OpenAPI-like surface for agent-driven, inventory-aware purchases, and (4) a heavy reliance on proxy-model visualization (See It On Your Model) rather than body-scanning or uploader-based personal-fit visualization. Amazon’s evidence shows a model-gallery, a single “Change model” control, and product-identity fidelity via model-rendered garments, but no shopper-body personalization through uploads. See annotated screenshots and source passages cited in the References for the exact UI and messaging observed.

value.value_proposition: OnPoint should position as a fit-aware supply graph for African fashion that ties real stock to local-pay-enabled agent workflows, enabling humans and AI agents to transact on the same inventory through a curator-driven model gallery and a transparent, regionally relevant payment/fulfillment flow (e.g., M-Pesa/WhatsApp in target markets) with explicit model-selection control and deterministic stock metadata.
value.what_onpoint_should_copy: Copy should emphasize: (a) the shopper can see the exact listed garment on a model chosen from a gallery of up to 40 real models, with a persistent selected-model state, (b) the system uses curator-supplied stock data and material specifics to support fit signals rather than uploading personal photos, (c) local payment and fulfillment options are integral to the confidence signal (e.g., M-Pesa/WhatsApp) and (d) a clear differentiation from generic ‘similar look’ generators by anchoring the experience to real SKUs, real stock, and real models tied to local supply ecosystems.
